Hi Priya — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and two asks so we can put together an accurate cost estimate: 

Summary from our side:
- BlueWave plans to embed summarization + context-aware search across ~3 product flows.
- Expected peak QPS per flow: 20, 10, and 5 respectively.
- Estimated prompt size (average user input + instructions + context) you mentioned: ~1,800 characters typical, up to 6,000 for heavy contexts.
- Monthly active users projected for pilot: 5k–15k.

Asks we ran through on the call and need clarified to finalize pricing: 
1) Are your volume estimates for "requests" actually API calls (i.e., HTTP requests) or end-user actions (one action can spawn multiple LLM requests)?
2) Are the numbers you quoted measured in characters, or have you already converted to tokens? We price by billed tokens; characters -> tokens conversion matters (approx 4 chars = 1 token for English but varies).
3) Do you expect to rely on our prompt/KV caching across repeated queries? That changes billed tokens vs network requests.

What I'll produce after we get those answers: a 3-month cost projection showing $/1M tokens target bands (conservative/expected/best case), and suggestions for prompt engineering + caching strategies to hit your budget targets.

Attaching the sample prompts you shared (redacted) and the rough volume spreadsheet — I annotated a couple of rows where token conversion makes big differences.

Next step: if you can reply with (a) whether "requests" == API calls, (b) if you have a character->token mapping you use, and (c) which flows are cacheable, I’ll send a tailored price band by EOD tomorrow.

Priya — perfect, that clears up a lot. I've turned the inputs you sent into token estimates (see inline). Two things I want to be explicit about because they commonly cause confusion: 

1) Tokens vs characters vs requests:
- Our billing is by billed tokens per model invocation. Characters are only useful as a heuristic; you should convert samples to tokens to get real estimates. For English, ~4 chars/token is a rough ballpark, but prompts with lots of code/emoji/foreign text differ.
- "Requests" = HTTP calls. Each request can consume many tokens in prompt + completion + KV cache fill. We recommend counting projected API calls per user action and multiplying by average tokens per call.

2) Prompt caching vs billed tokens:
- Caching reduces the number of full prompts you send to the model. If the request is served entirely from Redwood's prompt/KV cache, billed tokens can be close to zero (we bill only for cache-miss work and any completion tokens).
- However, partial caching (prefix cache) still bills for the uncached suffix + the completion. So cache hit rates need to be modeled at the request/token granularity.

Based on your samples and the flow breakdown you gave, I sketched three cost bands for a pilot month (converting characters -> tokens at 4 chars/token median):
- Conservative: 12M billed tokens/month -> cost est $1,080 per 1M tokens net (post-discount) -> $12,960/month.
- Expected: 38M billed tokens/month -> cost est $750 per 1M tokens -> $28,500/month.
- Optimistic: 110M billed tokens/month (with caching & batching) -> cost est $420 per 1M tokens -> $46,200/month.

Notes on the numbers:
- Those $/1M figures are illustrative per-model-band pricing (different models have different base per-token rates; I built these assuming a mix of a mid-size open LLM for most calls + a smaller reranker).
- Batching and KV caching are the levers that move you from 'conservative' to 'optimistic'. For example: if search achieves a 60% cache hit and is batched at 20 requests/batch, its token contribution drops significantly.

Next steps I propose: 
A) I'll prepare a one-page mutual action plan that lists the telemetry we need you to add (char counts -> token counts, request-per-action mapping, cache hit signals) so we can produce a precise 3-month cost forecast.
B) Optional technical check: have your eng team join a 30-min session with Karthik to go over caching hooks and token accounting (we can do Wed or Thu next week).

If those sound OK, I'll send the MAP and cost spreadsheet. Also happy to convert the per-month pilot numbers to an ARR-equivalent so your finance folks can map to the $250–400k target.

Thanks — Alex

On a related note, Karthik added a quick math sample in the XLS to show how a 1% token drop in prompts scales across 100M tokens — might be helpful for leadership to see marginal savings.

--

Subject: Re: Quick recap + pricing metric Qs (tokens vs chars vs requests)

Priya — quick intro from me, I'll run the tech session if you'd like. A couple of practical items that engineering teams often miss when converting characters to billed tokens: 

1) Tokenization variance: run a 1k-sample through the exact tokenizer used by the serving model (I'll share a small script) — this avoids systematic under/over-estimates.
2) Prefix vs suffix caching: store large static context in KV cache (we bill KV fills once), and send only the variable suffix. That can reduce billed tokens per request by 30–70% depending on context size.
3) Batching latency vs cost tradeoff: we can configure continuous batching with latency SLOs; I can simulate the expected latency impact for your QPS numbers and tune batch windows to hit the desired $/1M token goal.

If you're ok, I'll pencil in a 30-min tech sync for Thu 2026-04-22 10:00 PT and share the tokenizer script + a small cost-sim template.
